Reasoning:

1. A di-substituted benzene ring supplies C6H4 (only two aromatic hydrogens are seen, agreeing with the ¹H-NMR).

2. One substituent must be an ester group.  The simplest aryl ester that contains no CH₂ protons is an acetoxy group –OCOCH₃, whose formula is C₂H₃O₂ (2 carbons, 3 hydrogens, 2 oxygens).

3. The other substituent provides:
   • two vinyl protons (signals: one doublet, one doublet-of-quartets),
   • one methyl group coupled to those vinyl protons,
   • no CH₂ protons.

   The fragment CH₂=C(CH₃)– (isopropenyl) fits this: it has two nonequivalent vinyl H’s (giving d and dq) and one methyl that couples to one of them, with formula C₃H₅.

4. Adding the fragments:
   Benzene core: C₆H₄  
   Isopropenyl:   + C₃H₅  
   Acetoxy:     + C₂H₃O₂  
   --------------------------------  
   Total:       C₁₁H₁₂O₂

5. Calculate the degrees of unsaturation:
   DU = (2C + 2 – H)/2 = (2·11 + 2 – 12)/2 = (24 – 12)/2 = 6.
   A benzene ring (4 DU) + one C=C (1 DU) + one C=O (1 DU) = 6, in full agreement.

Thus the only formula consistent with all the spectral data is C11H12O2.

Answer: C
